plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you never overpay since you only pay the second-highest bid, and bidding truthfully maximizes expected profit regardless of competitors' strategies. Bidding below value risks losing profitable auctions; bidding above value risks negative profit. With value $25, the optimal bid is exactly $25.

In a second-price auction (winner pays second-highest bid), bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of opponents' strategies. This is because if I bid below my value, I risk losing auctions I could have profitably won; if I bid above my value, I risk winning at a price higher than my value, causing a loss. Since payment depends only on the second-highest bid (not my own bid, given I win), bidding exactly my value maximizes expected profit. With value $31, I will bid $31.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of the number of bidders or their strategies. This is because you pay the second-highest bid if you win, not your own bid, so bidding your true value maximizes expected profit without risk of overpaying or leaving money on the table. With a value of $9, I should bid exactly $9.
